subject: General Knowledge
description: Covers Emblem, Flag Code, Anthem, Song, Scientific names, and Saka Calendar.

questions.stem: The National Emblem of India is an adaptation of the Lion Capital of Ashoka. Which of the following animals is NOT depicted on the circular abacus of the emblem?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The abacus (the circular base) of the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath features four animals separated by intervening wheels (Chakras). The four animals are: an Elephant (representing Queen Maya's conception dream), a Bull (representing Taurus, the month of Buddha's birth), a Horse (representing Kanthaka, the horse Buddha rode when he departed his palace), and a Lion (representing the attainment of enlightenment). The Tiger is NOT present.
DECOY BUSTING: While the Bengal Tiger is the National Animal of India, it does not feature on the National Emblem. 
EXAM INSIGHT: In the two-dimensional official representation of the National Emblem adopted by the Government of India on 26 January 1950, only three lions are visible. On the abacus, the galloping Horse is visible on the left, the Bull on the right, and the Dharma Chakra in the center. The words "Satyameva Jayate" (Truth Alone Triumphs) from the Mundaka Upanishad are inscribed below in Devanagari script.

questions.stem: Who composed the National Anthem of India, 'Jana Gana Mana'?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: Rabindranath Tagore, the Nobel Laureate polymath, composed "Jana Gana Mana" originally in Bengali as "Bharoto Bhagyo Bidhata". The Hindi version was adopted by the Constituent Assembly as the National Anthem of India on 24 January 1950.
DECOY BUSTING: Bankim Chandra Chatterjee composed "Vande Mataram", which is the National Song of India. Muhammad Iqbal wrote "Sare Jahan Se Achha".
EXAM INSIGHT: "Jana Gana Mana" was first publicly sung on 27 December 1911 at the Calcutta Session of the Indian National Congress. Tagore holds the unique distinction of having his compositions adopted as the national anthems of two countries: India and Bangladesh ("Amar Shonar Bangla").

questions.stem: According to the Flag Code of India, what is the prescribed ratio of the length to the height (width) of the National Flag?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Flag Code of India strictly specifies that the National Flag shall be rectangular in shape, and the ratio of the length to the height (width) of the Flag shall be 3:2. 
DECOY BUSTING: 2:1 is the ratio for the flags of the UK and Canada. 1:1 is a square (like Switzerland). 
EXAM INSIGHT: The National Flag was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on 22 July 1947. The design was based on the Swaraj flag designed by Pingali Venkayya. The Ashoka Chakra in the center must have 24 spokes and be in navy blue color, representing the "wheel of the law of dharma" and continuous motion/progress.

questions.stem: From which ancient text is the national motto 'Satyameva Jayate' (Truth alone triumphs) taken?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: "Satyameva Jayate" is a mantra from the ancient Indian text, the Mundaka Upanishad (specifically, Mantra 3.1.6). Following the independence of India, it was adopted as the national motto of India on 26 January 1950. It is inscribed in the Devanagari script at the base of the Lion Capital of Ashoka and forms an integral part of the Indian National Emblem.
DECOY BUSTING: The Rig Veda is the oldest Veda (contains the Gayatri Mantra). The Katha Upanishad contains the famous story of Nachiketa and Yama. The Bhagavad Gita is part of the Mahabharata.
EXAM INSIGHT: Questions asking to match philosophical concepts to specific Upanishads are very common in UPSC. Remember: Mundaka = Satyameva Jayate; Mandukya = Om and the four states of consciousness; Brihadaranyaka = 'Asato ma sadgamaya' (Lead me from falsehood to truth).

questions.stem: Which of the following dates marks the adoption of 'Vande Mataram' as the National Song of India by the Constituent Assembly, giving it equal status with the National Anthem?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: On 24 January 1950 (the final session of the Constituent Assembly), Dr. Rajendra Prasad, the President of the Assembly, declared that "Vande Mataram" would be honored equally with "Jana Gana Mana" and have equal status as the National Song. 
DECOY BUSTING: 22 July 1947 was the adoption of the National Flag. 26 January 1950 was the commencement of the Constitution and the adoption of the National Emblem.
EXAM INSIGHT: "Vande Mataram" was written in Sanskrit-Bengali by Bankim Chandra Chatterjee in his 1882 novel 'Anandamath' (which is set against the backdrop of the Sannyasi Rebellion). It was first sung in a political context by Rabindranath Tagore at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress.

questions.stem: What is the scientific name of the National Flower of India, the Lotus?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The scientific name of the Indian Lotus, the National Flower, is Nelumbo nucifera. It is an aquatic herb that holds immense cultural, religious, and mythological significance in both Hinduism and Buddhism, symbolizing purity, achievement, and long life.
DECOY BUSTING: Ficus benghalensis is the Banyan tree (National Tree). Panthera tigris is the Bengal Tiger (National Animal). Pavo cristatus is the Indian Peafowl/Peacock (National Bird).
EXAM INSIGHT: State and SSC exams often test the scientific names of national symbols to increase the difficulty of basic questions. Remember that the Ganges River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica) is the National Aquatic Animal, and the King Cobra (Ophiophagus hannah) is the National Reptile.

questions.stem: The Saka Calendar was introduced as the Indian National Calendar in 1957 alongside the Gregorian calendar. The Saka era began in which year?
questions.explanation:
WHY IT IS CORRECT: The Saka Era was founded in 78 AD, historically associated with the accession of the Kushana king Kanishka (though scholars debate the exact origins). The Government of India adopted the Saka Calendar as the National Calendar on 22 March 1957. 
DECOY BUSTING: 58 BC marks the beginning of the Vikram Samvat (another highly popular Hindu calendar). 319 AD marks the Gupta Era. 622 AD marks the Hijri (Islamic) calendar, beginning with the Prophet's migration to Medina.
EXAM INSIGHT: The National Calendar begins with the month of Chaitra, which normally starts on 22 March (or 21 March in a leap year). The months are Chaitra, Vaisakha, Jyaistha, Asadha, Sravana, Bhadra, Asvina, Kartika, Agrahayana, Pausa, Magha, and Phalguna. A standard year has 365 days, perfectly synchronized with the Gregorian calendar.

questions.stem: Which animal was officially declared the National Aquatic Animal of India in October 2009?
questions.explanation: The Gangetic River Dolphin (Platanista gangetica) was declared National Aquatic Animal in October 2009 to highlight its conservation importance in the Ganga river system. The Gharial is the National Reptile, not the aquatic animal. The Irrawaddy Dolphin is found in the Chilika Lake region but was never given this designation.

questions.stem: What is the correct scientific name of India's National Tree, the Indian Banyan?

options.option_text: Ficus religiosa (the Peepal, sacred fig of India)
Ficus benghalensis (Indian Banyan, the national tree)
Tectona grandis (Teak, India's premier timber species)
Azadirachta indica (Neem, used in Ayurvedic medicine)

questions.explanation: Ficus benghalensis (Indian Banyan) is the National Tree. The most common wrong answer is Ficus religiosa (Peepal), which is sacred in Buddhist and Hindu traditions but is NOT the national tree. The Banyan was chosen because its vast, spreading canopy symbolises unity and the country's deep roots.

questions.stem: The drum (abacus) of the Lion Capital of Sarnath — adapted as India's National Emblem — depicts four animals interspersed with Dharma Chakras. Which of the following animals is NOT depicted on that abacus?

options.option_text: Bull (symbolising strength and the Dharmic order)

questions.explanation: The four animals carved on the abacus are Horse, Bull, Elephant, and Lion — each separated by a Dharma Chakra. The Deer does NOT appear on the abacus. Deer are associated with the Sarnath site (Deer Park) and Buddhist iconography, which makes this a high-quality distractor that misleads many candidates.

questions.stem: The Flag Code of India specifies a precise colour for the Ashoka Chakra printed at the centre of the National Flag. Which colour is mandated?

options.option_text: Black, as seen on the original Sarnath stone pillar
Golden yellow, matching ancient Ashoka-era artistic tradition
Navy blue, representing the wheel of cosmic law
Dark indigo, symbolising the depth of Indian civilisation

questions.explanation: The Flag Code of India mandates that the Ashoka Chakra be printed in Navy Blue on both sides of the flag. Golden yellow is a tempting distractor because it evokes the colour of the original carved stone and the orange stripe, but the actual specification is navy blue. The Chakra has 24 spokes representing the 24 hours of the day.

questions.stem: In which year was the Indian Elephant officially designated as India's National Heritage Animal by the Government of India?

options.option_text: 2008, under the amended Wildlife Protection Act provisions
2010, declared by the Ministry of Environment and Forests
2012, to mark the twentieth anniversary of Project Elephant
2014, announced during the National Wildlife Week celebrations

questions.explanation: The Indian Elephant was designated National Heritage Animal on 22 October 2010 by the Ministry of Environment and Forests to strengthen its legal protection and conservation status. Project Elephant itself was launched in 1992, making 2012 a plausible but incorrect distractor.

questions.stem: The Indian Rupee symbol (₹), officially adopted in July 2010, is a visual fusion of letters from which two scripts?

options.option_text: Tamil script 'Ru' blended with the Roman capital letter 'R'
Devanagari 'Ra' (र) merged with Roman 'R' with two horizontal bars
Telugu script 'Ru' blended with the Roman capital letter 'E'
Bengali script 'Ra' merged with a modified Roman letter 'P'

questions.explanation: The ₹ symbol was designed by D. Udaya Kumar (IIT Bombay) and merges the Devanagari letter 'र' (Ra) with the Roman 'R' stripped of its vertical stroke, topped by two parallel horizontal bars representing equality. Tamil-script origin is a popular misconception because the designer is from Tamil Nadu, but the Devanagari element is definitively part of the official design rationale.

questions.stem: On which exact date was 'Jana Gana Mana' formally adopted as India's National Anthem, and at which session was it first sung publicly before Independence?

options.option_text: 26 January 1950; first sung at Calcutta Congress session, December 1911
24 January 1950; first sung at Calcutta Congress session, December 1911
15 August 1947; first sung at the Lahore Congress session, December 1929
26 November 1949; first sung at the Nagpur Congress session, December 1920

questions.explanation: Jana Gana Mana was officially adopted as the National Anthem on 24 January 1950 — two days before the Republic was proclaimed. It was first sung publicly on 27 December 1911 at the Calcutta (Kolkata) session of the Indian National Congress. The most common error is confusing this date with 26 January 1950 (Republic Day) or with 1929 (the Lahore Congress is associated with the Purna Swaraj resolution, not the anthem).
